title: Coding is finally done on Where Is My Home? RPG Sim – handcrafted since 2019, ~$15 total budget.
author: Sea_Intention9648
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I’m officially calling the coding phase complete for Where Is My Home? RPG Sim, only the writing and localization left now. I’ve set the release date for February 28, 2027 (mostly to get the legal side sorted), so I figured I’d drop one last little showcase video in the meantime. :)

The game's art style is inspired by children's drawings, as the story takes place inside the inner universe of a grieving child's mind and the project itself was born out of a very similar personal pain.

The entire project cost me around $15, which literally went toward replacement nibs for my Wacom pen display. Sure, time is money, but since software development is my job, it mattered way more to me to truly understand everything under the hood, build skills I can directly apply in my career, and know that I engineered the whole thing myself.

Tools & Tech Stack:

Art & Animation: Started on a Wacom Intuos S, later upgraded to a Wacom One 14; created in Moho 14 and Clip Studio Paint.

Backend: C#, Redis, SignalR, Seq, PostgreSQL

Frontend: Ionic Angular, PixiJS

Ingame sound and vfx: Custom record and garage band. 

I built this with pure, "handcrafted" code starting back in 2019. About six months ago, I started using a small local 14B LLM, mostly just to bounce off or generate trickiet yet still relatively straightforward—helper methods.

At the end of the day, I just hope people enjoy playing it half as much as I loved making it.

comments.author: PavlovicProd
comments.body:
The $15 budget is insane given the scope. You're essentially doing R&D on your own time for a side project while managing full-time PM duties across time zones, which is a massive commitment. 

  
Since you mentioned using a local LLM for helper methods rather than core logic, that's a solid approach for keeping costs down. It prevents you from hitting API rate limits or incurring unexpected cloud bills as the codebase grows. Just be careful with the generated code quality; I've seen too many fintech MVPs break because a model hallucinated a security check or payment validation step that looked correct but wasn't.

replies.author: Sea_Intention9648
replies.body:
Thank you very much! Yes this is my job, my life, and my hobbies! : ) 

No, no it doesn't have write permissions at all. I review every method myself and manually put it where it belongs. Sadly, I can't name where I'm seeing it firsthand, but "vibe-coding" is causing a massive mess and leaving behind completely unsustainable codebases—forcing people to eventually switch over to paying for expensive APIs just to keep things afloat.
